text:
Method: the isothermal compressible pipe-flow equation with the acceleration term included is
p1² − p2² = G² (RT/M) [ f·L/D + 2 ln(p1/p2) ]
Re = G·D/μ = 4ṁ/(π D μ), which is constant along the pipe.

Numbers:
- RT/M = 8314 × 288 / 16.04 = 1.4928×10⁵ J/kg.
- p1² − p2² = 25×10¹² − 9×10¹² = 16×10¹² Pa².
- L/D = 40000 / 0.30 = 1.3333×10⁵.
- 2 ln(5/3) = 1.0217.
- ε/D = 0.046×10⁻³ / 0.30 = 1.533×10⁻⁴.
- Pipe area A = π/4 × 0.30² = 0.070686 m².

Iteration (f and Re are coupled through G):
1. Start with f ≈ 0.0135. Then G² = 16×10¹² / [1.4928×10⁵ × (1800 + 1.02)], so G ≈ 244 kg/m²s and Re ≈ 6.65×10⁶.
2. Colebrook: 1/√f = −2 log10[ (ε/D)/3.7 + 2.51/(Re √f) ], with (ε/D)/3.7 = 4.144×10⁻⁵.
3. At Re ≈ 6.7×10⁶ this gives 1/√f ≈ 8.70, so f ≈ 0.01321.
4. With f = 0.01321: f·L/D = 1761.7, and the bracket is 1761.7 + 1.02 = 1762.7.
5. G² = 16×10¹² / (1.4928×10⁵ × 1762.7) = 6.081×10⁴, so G = 246.6 kg/m²s.
6. Re = 246.6 × 0.30 / 1.1×10⁻⁵ = 6.73×10⁶. Re-evaluating Colebrook at this Re gives f = 0.01321 again, so the iteration has converged.

(a) ṁ = G·A = 246.6 × 0.070686 = 17.4 kg/s.
(b) Re = 6.73×10⁶.
(c) f = 0.0132 (Colebrook, 0.01321).
(d) Outlet density ρ2 = p2 M/(RT) = 3×10⁶ / 1.4928×10⁵ = 20.10 kg/m³. Outlet velocity v2 = G/ρ2 = 246.6 / 20.10 = 12.3 m/s.

I did this by hand with no tools and no code, so the numbers are not checked by a program.

FINAL (a): 17.4 kg/s
FINAL (b): 6.73e6 (dimensionless)
FINAL (c): 0.0132 (dimensionless)
FINAL (d): 12.3 m/s
